findings.title: Shinhan Bank hit by data breach affecting 25,000 customers
findings.summary_md: First same-day English coverage of the incident, six days before CrowdStrike framed the campaign as AI-driven. Shinhan Bank apologized after a breach exposed data on about 25,000 customers, including names, phone numbers, annual income, loan eligibility limits, 66 cases involving resident registration numbers and 97 cases of connected information. The bank said an unauthorized external party bypassed authentication, and the Financial Supervisory Service conducted an on-site inspection.

findings.title: (LEAD) Some 25,000 customers' info leaked from Shinhan Bank in apparent AI agent-assisted hacking
findings.summary_md: Yonhap's lead wire, published the day after the September 30 leak, reports loan records, annual income, names and phone numbers taken from Shinhan's loan borrowing service. Sources said the hackers, suspected to be based overseas, used advanced AI tools, and experts assessed the bank was not specifically targeted but caught in random AI-powered attacks against vulnerable online platforms. This is the earliest reporting of the AI angle that predates the campaign attribution.

findings.title: AI Tools Suspected in Korea's Shinhan Bank Hack, Yonhap News Reports
findings.summary_md: First substantial international pickup, citing Yonhap: AI agents probably probed for vulnerabilities and accessed a service used by loan recruiters. It already connects the Shinhan breach to smaller leaks at KB Kookmin (119 customers) and Hana Bank (89 customers) and to the Financial Services Commission's meetings with local banks. Genians director Mun Chong-hyun warned that AI tools shared for defensive purposes become a double-edged sword in hacking attempts.

findings.title: ARTEX: A Self-Hosted Autonomous Penetration Testing System Written in Go
findings.summary_md: Independent write-up of the ARTEX project by GitHub user Autumn-27, published four days before the campaign attribution. It documents an open-source autonomous penetration testing system pairing a Go backend with a Next.js frontend under AGPL-3.0, winner of Baidu's agent+ attack-defense challenge, with 1,450 stars and 261 forks at the time of writing. The piece covers approval-gated agent actions, traffic recording, deployment via Docker image autumn27/artex or a single binary, and a UI on port 8787.

findings.title: Open-Source AI Agent Hacked Seven South Korean Banks, Exposing 65,000 Records
findings.summary_md: Two days before this story's first sighting, TechTimes reported the Financial Security Institute confirmed the ARTEX link after tracing attack IP addresses and server logs from Shinhan Bank, the first institution to report. The forensic artifact was the string `ARTEX-自主渗透测试控制台`, roughly autonomous penetration testing console, found in the HTML title of a server used in the campaign. It reported attackers spent up to 43 hours undetected, more than 65,000 customers exposed across seven institutions, and a round-the-clock national cybersecurity emergency response activated on October 5.
